questions.q: A monochromatic source of light operating at $15$ kW emits $2.5\times 10^{22}$ photons/s. The region of an electromagnetic spectrum to which the emitted electromagnetic radiation belongs to ________. (Take $h=6.6\times 10^{-34}$ J·s and $c=3\times 10^8$ m/s).
questions.solution:
Power of the source, $P = 15 \text{ kW} = 15 \times 10^3 \text{ J/s}$

Number of photons emitted per second, $n = 2.5 \times 10^{22} \text{ s}^{-1}$

Energy of one photon, $E = \dfrac{P}{n} = \dfrac{15 \times 10^3}{2.5 \times 10^{22}} = 6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$

Using $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, we get $\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{E}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{6 \times 10^{-19}} = 3.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 330 \text{ nm}$

The wavelength $330 \text{ nm}$ lies in the ultraviolet region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Answer: Ultraviolet

questions.q: For an electromagnetic wave propagating through vacuum, $\vec{k}$, $\vec{E}$ and $\omega$ represent propagation vector, electric field and angular frequency, respectively. The magnetic field associated with this wave is represented by :
questions.solution:
For an electromagnetic wave, the direction of wave propagation $\hat{k}$ is along the direction of $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Since $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$, and $\vec{k}$ form a mutually perpendicular right-handed system, the direction of the magnetic field is given by $\hat{B} = \hat{k} \times \hat{E}$.

The magnitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $B = \dfrac{E}{c}$.

Using the relation for the speed of light $c = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$, we get $B = \dfrac{kE}{\omega}$.

Combining the magnitude and direction gives:

$\vec{B} = B\hat{B} = \dfrac{kE}{\omega} (\hat{k} \times \hat{E})$

Since $\vec{k} = k\hat{k}$ and $\vec{E} = E\hat{E}$, this simplifies to:

$\vec{B} = \dfrac{\vec{k} \times \vec{E}}{\omega}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\vec{k} \times \vec{E}}{\omega}$

questions.q: A point light source emits E.M. waves in free space. A detector, placed at a distance of $L$ m, measures the intensity as $I_o$. The detector is now shifted to another location on the same spherical surface ensuring the angle between original location and new location as $45°$. The measured intensity at new location will be _______.
questions.solution:
For a point light source, the intensity of electromagnetic waves at a distance $r$ is given by $I = \dfrac{P}{4\pi r^2}$, where $P$ is the power of the source.

Since the detector is moved to a new location on the same spherical surface, the distance from the source remains $L$.

The emission from a point source is isotropic, meaning the intensity depends only on the radial distance from the source and is independent of the angular position.

Therefore, the intensity at the new location remains unchanged, which is $I_o$.

Answer: $I_o$

questions.q: A displacement current of $4.0$ A can be set up in the space between two parallel plates of $6$\mu$F capacitor. The rate of change of potential difference across the plates of the capacitor is nearly $\alpha \times 10^6$ V/s. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.solution:
The displacement current $I_d$ between the plates of a capacitor is given by the formula:

$I_d = C \dfrac{dV}{dt}$

Substituting the given values of displacement current and capacitance:

$4.0 = 6 \times 10^{-6} \times \dfrac{dV}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{4.0}{6 \times 10^{-6}}$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 10^6 \approx 0.67 \times 10^6$ V/s

Comparing this with the given rate of change of potential difference $\alpha \times 10^6$ V/s, we get $\alpha = 0.67$.

Answer: $0.67$

questions.q: A magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave is represented by $\vec{B}=B_0\sin\left(2\pi vt-\dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\hat{j}$. Its associated electric field vector is ______.
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is determined by the phase term $2\pi vt - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda}$, which indicates that the wave is travelling along the $+x$ direction ($\hat{i}$).

The direction of the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given as $\hat{j}$.

In an electromagnetic wave, the direction of propagation is given by the direction of the cross product $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Let the direction of the electric field $\vec{E}$ be $\hat{n}$.

$\hat{n} \times \hat{j} = \hat{i}$

Since $(-\hat{k}) \times \hat{j} = \hat{i}$, the direction of the electric field must be $-\hat{k}$.

The amplitude of the electric field is related to the magnetic field by $E_0 = c B_0$, where $c$ is the speed of the wave.

The speed of the wave is $c = v \lambda$, where $v$ is the frequency.

$E_0 = v \lambda B_0$

Therefore, the electric field vector is $\vec{E} = -v \lambda B_0 \sin\left(2\pi vt - \dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right) \hat{k}$.

Answer: $\vec{E}=-v\lambda B_0\sin\left(2\pi vt-\dfrac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\hat{k}$

Therefore, the electric field vector is $\vec{E} = -60 \hat{k}$ V/m.

Answer: $-60 \hat{k}$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travelling in $x$-direction is described by field equation $E_y = 300\sin\omega\left(t - \dfrac{x}{c}\right)$. If the electron is restricted to move in $y$-direction only with speed of $1.5 \times 10^6$ m/s then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is _______.
questions.solution:
The maximum electric force acting on the electron is $F_e = eE_0$.

The maximum magnetic force acting on the electron is $F_m = evB_0$, where $v$ is the speed of the electron and $B_0$ is the maximum magnetic field.

The ratio of the maximum electric force to the maximum magnetic force is given by $\dfrac{F_e}{F_m} = \dfrac{eE_0}{evB_0} = \dfrac{E_0}{vB_0}$.

For an electromagnetic wave, the ratio of the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields is $\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = c$, where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum.

Substituting this into the ratio of forces yields $\dfrac{F_e}{F_m} = \dfrac{c}{v}$.

Given $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s and $v = 1.5 \times 10^6$ m/s, we get $\dfrac{F_e}{F_m} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^6} = 200$.

Answer: $200$

The magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ of the wave is:

For an electromagnetic wave, the relationship between electric and magnetic field amplitudes is $B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c}$.
Here $E_0 = 54$ V/m and $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s.
So, $B_0 = \frac{54}{3 \times 10^8} = 1.8 \times 10^{-7}$ T.
The electric field is along the $\hat{j}$ direction.

Using the right-hand rule: $\hat{j} \times (-\hat{i}) = \hat{k}$ (positive $z$ direction), confirming the magnetic field is in the $-\hat{i}$ direction.
Therefore, $\vec{B} = -1.8 \times 10^{-7}\sin(kz - \omega t)\hat{i}$ T.

Therefore, $n = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{2.0 \times 10^8} = 1.5$

questions.q:
The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant $k=3$ and permeability of $\mu=2 \mu_{0}$, is
($\mu_{0}=$ permeability of vacuum)
questions.solution:
Speed of electromagnetic wave in vacuum: $c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$
Speed in a medium with permeability $\mu = 2\mu_0$ and dielectric constant $k = 3$:
$v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \epsilon}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\mu_0 \times 3\epsilon_0}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6\mu_0\epsilon_0}}$
$v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}} = \frac{c}{\sqrt{6}}$
Ratio of speeds: $\frac{c}{v} = \sqrt{6}$
Therefore: $c : v = \sqrt{6} : 1$

The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : $E=\sqrt{377} \sin \left(6.27 \times 10^{3} t-2.09 \times 10^{-5} x\right) \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{C}$
The average power of the electromagnetic wave is $\left(\frac{1}{\alpha}\right) \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$
(Take $\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\varepsilon_{o}}}=377$ in SI units)

From the electric field equation, amplitude:
$E_0 = \sqrt{377}$ N/C
Average intensity of EM wave:
$I_{avg} = \frac{E_0^2}{2Z_0}$ where $Z_0 = \sqrt{\mu_0/\varepsilon_0} = 377$ Ω
$I_{avg} = \frac{(\sqrt{377})^2}{2 \times 377} = \frac{377}{2 \times 377} = \frac{1}{2}$ W/m²
Given $I_{avg} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$ W/m², we have $\frac{1}{\alpha} = \frac{1}{2}$
Therefore, $\alpha = 2$

The average power of the electromagnetic wave is $\left(\frac{1}{\alpha}\right) \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$
(Take $\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\varepsilon_{o}}}=377$ in SI units)
questions.explanation:
From the electric field equation, amplitude:
$E_0 = \sqrt{377}$ N/C
Average intensity of EM wave:
$I_{avg} = \frac{E_0^2}{2Z_0}$ where $Z_0 = \sqrt{\mu_0/\varepsilon_0} = 377$ Ω
$I_{avg} = \frac{(\sqrt{377})^2}{2 \times 377} = \frac{377}{2 \times 377} = \frac{1}{2}$ W/m²
Given $I_{avg} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$ W/m², we have $\frac{1}{\alpha} = \frac{1}{2}$
Therefore, $\alpha = 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A laser beam has intensity of $4.0 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is $\_\_\_\_$ T.
(Take $\epsilon_{\mathrm{o}}=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^{2} / \mathrm{Nm}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$)
questions.solution:
The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is
$I = \frac{1}{2} \epsilon_0 c E_0^2$.
From the relation $E_0 = c B_0$, we get $I = \frac{1}{2} \epsilon_0 c^3 B_0^2$.
Solving for magnetic field amplitude:
$B_0 = \sqrt{\frac{2I}{\epsilon_0 c^3}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 4.0 \times 10^{14}}{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times (3 \times 10^8)^3}} = \sqrt{\frac{8.0 \times 10^{14}}{2.39 \times 10^{14}}}$
$= \sqrt{3.347} = 1.83$ T.

From the wave equation $E_y = 20\sin(3 \times 10^6 x - 4.5 \times 10^{14} t)$:
Wave number: $k = 3 \times 10^6$ m⁻¹
Angular frequency: $\omega = 4.5 \times 10^{14}$ rad/s
Speed of wave in medium: $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{4.5 \times 10^{14}}{3 \times 10^6} = 1.5 \times 10^8$ m/s
Speed of light in vacuum: $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s
Refractive index: $n = \frac{c}{v} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^8} = 2$
For a nonmagnetic medium: $n = \sqrt{\epsilon_r}$
Dielectric constant: $\epsilon_r = n^2 = 4$

questions.q:
An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, $\sigma=10 \mathrm{mho} / \mathrm{m}$. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is $\_\_\_\_$.
$\left[\text{Take }\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{\mathrm{o}}}=9 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{Nm}^{2} / \mathrm{C}^{2}\right]$
questions.solution:
For an electromagnetic wave in a conducting medium, the maximum conduction current density is $J_{c,max} = \sigma E_0$ and maximum displacement current density is $J_{d,max} = \epsilon_0 \omega E_0$.
The ratio is: $\frac{J_{c,max}}{J_{d,max}} = \frac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0 \omega}$.
With $\sigma = 10$ mho/m, $f = 100$ MHz
So $\omega = 2\pi \times 10^8$ rad/s, and $\epsilon_0 = \frac{10^{-9}}{36\pi}$ F/m: $\frac{J_{c,max}}{J_{d,max}} = \frac{10 \times 36\pi}{10^{-9} \times 2\pi \times 10^8} = \frac{10 \times 36}{2 \times 10^{-1}} = 1800$.

questions.solution:
Given $E_y = 69 \sin[0.6 \times 10^3 x - 1.8 \times 10^{11} t]$ V/m
Wave propagates along +x (form $kx - \omega t$), $\vec{E}$ is along y.
For EM wave: $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ = direction of propagation

$B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c} = \frac{69}{3 \times 10^8} = 2.3 \times 10^{-7}$ T
E and B are in phase for plane EM wave.
$B_z = 2.3 \times 10^{-7} \sin[0.6 \times 10^3 x - 1.8 \times 10^{11} t]$ T

Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{E}_1=\mathrm{E}_0 \sin \omega \mathrm{t} \\ & \mathrm{E}_2=\mathrm{E}_0 \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\end{aligned}$
Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{E}=\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)^2+\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)^2+2\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right)\left(\mathrm{E}_0\right) \cos \frac{\pi}{3}}$

questions.q:
If an optical medium possesses a relative permeability of $\frac{10}{\pi}$ and relative permittivity of $\frac{1}{0.0885}$, then the velocity of light is greater in vacuum than that in this medium by ________ times.
$\left(\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{H} / \mathrm{m}, \epsilon_0=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}\right.$
$\left.\mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$
questions.solution:
Since velocity of light in terms of $\mu \& E$ is
$\begin{aligned}
& V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \epsilon}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \mu_r}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\epsilon_0 \epsilon_r}} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{r}} \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}} \\ & =\frac{C}{\sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{r}} \epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}}}=\frac{C}{\sqrt{\frac{10}{\pi} \times \frac{1}{0.0885}}} \\ & =\frac{C}{\sqrt{36}}=\frac{C}{6}
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{V} & =\frac{\mathrm{C}}{6} \\ \mathrm{C} & =6 \mathrm{~V}
\end{aligned}$
Velocity of light in vacuum is greater by 6 times the velocity of light in medium
Answer is 6

In an electromagnetic wave, the direction of energy flow is along the direction of the wave propagation. Therefore, the wave propagates along negative z direction.

$( - \overset{^}{k} ) = ( + \overset{^}{j} ) \times \left(\overset{^}{i}\right)$

Hence, magnetic field is in positive $x$ direction.

Given, ${E}_{y} = 900sin\left(\omegat - \dfrac{\omegax}{c}\right)$

Here, ${E}_{0} = 900$

questions.solution:
The intensity is defined as energy per unit time per unit area. Therefore, $I = \dfrac{dE}{Adt}$.

Energy density is energy per unit volume. Therefore, ${U}_{d} = \dfrac{dE}{Adx}$.

Dividing $\dfrac{I}{{U}_{d}} = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = c$

$⇒ {U}_{d} = \dfrac{I}{c} = \dfrac{0 . 22}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{22}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$

Magnetic energy density will be half of total energy density, Therefore, ${U}_{b} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$.

Now energy density in magnetic field is given by, ${U}_{b} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}}{2{\mu}_{0}}$. Therefore,

${B}_{rms}^{2}2{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$ where ${B}_{rms}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{{B}_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = {B}_{0}^{2}2$

$⇒ {B}_{0}^{2}4{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10} ⇒ {B}_{0} = \sqrt{4 \times \left(4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\right) \times \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}} ⇒ {B}_{0} = 4 . 29 \times {10}^{- 8}T ≃ 43 \times {10}^{- 9}T$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: A time varying electric field is a source of changing magnetic field and vice-versa. Thus a disturbance in electric or magnetic field creates EM waves.

Statement II: In a material medium, the EM wave travels with speed $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{\mu}_{0}{ϵ}_{0}}}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true
questions.solution:
According to the Maxwell’s EM theory, the EM waves propagation contains electric and magnetic field vibration in mutually perpendicular direction. Thus, the changing of electric field give rise to magnetic field.

Also, time varying magnetic field produces electric field. According to Faradays law, when magnetic flux changes in the region surrounded by conductor, it produces electric field (induced emf) in conductor.

In a material medium the EM wave travels with speed given by $\begin{cases}v & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\muε}} \\ v & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{{\mu}_{0}{\mu}_{r}( {ε}_{0}{ε}_{r} )}}\end{cases}$

Thus, statement I is correct but statement II is false.

At $t = 0s,$ two electric charges ${q}_{1}$ of $4\pi$ coulomb and ${q}_{2}$ of $2\pi$ coulomb located at $\left(0, 0, \dfrac{\pi}{k}\right)$ and $\left(0, 0, \dfrac{3\pi}{k}\right),$ respectively, have the same velocity of $0 . 5c\overset{^}{i},$ (where $c$ is the velocity of light ). The ratio of the force acting on charge ${q}_{1}$ to ${q}_{2}$ is :
questions.solution:
At $t = 0$
$B$ at $\left(0, 0, \dfrac{\pi}{k}\right) = {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)cos\left(\pi\right)$
$B$ at $\left(0, 0, \dfrac{3\pi}{k}\right) = {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)cos\left(3\pi\right)$
Force on charged particle ${q}_{1}$
${F}_{1} = {q}_{1}\overset{\to}{V}1 \times \overset{\to}{B}1$
$= 4\pi\left(0 . 5c\overset{^}{i}\right) \times \left[- {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right] = \dfrac{4\pi{B}_{0}c}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$
Force on charged particle ${q}_{2}$
${F}_{2} = {q}_{2}\overset{\to}{V}2 \times \overset{\to}{B}2$
$= 2\pi\left(0 . 5c\overset{^}{i}\right) \times \left[- {B}_{0}\left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right] = \dfrac{2\pi{B}_{0}c}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{{F}_{1}}{{F}_{2}} = 2$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $3GHz$ enters a dielectric medium of relative electric permittivity $2 . 25$ from vacuum. The wavelength of this wave in that medium will be _________ $\times {10}^{- 2}cm .$

$∴ \lambda$ in medium $= \dfrac{0 . 1}{\mu}$

Where refractive index

$∴ \mu = \sqrt{2 . 25} = 1 . 5$

$= 667 \times {10}^{- 2}cm$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $5GHz$, is travelling in a medium whose relative electric permittivity and relative magnetic permeability both are $2 .$ Its velocity in this medium is _______$\times {10}^{7}m{s}^{- 1}$.

Given : Frequency of wave $f = 5GHz$

$= 5 \times {10}^{9}Hz$

Where $C$ is speed of light is vacuum

$∴ v = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{30 \times {10}^{7}}{2}m{s}^{- 1}$

$= 15 \times {10}^{7}m{s}^{- 1}$

$∴$ Ans. is $15$

questions.solution:
Polarization of EM Wave means Direction of Its electric Field

Electric field vector is along $\overset{^}{k}$

Direction of wave,$\overset{^}{c} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$ (Given)

$\overset{^}{B} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}} \times \overset{^}{k} = \dfrac{\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$

General Form is $B = ( {B}_{0}\overset{^}{B} ) cos\left(\omegat - \overset{^}{c}k\right)$

where ${B}_{0}$ is Magnitude of Magnetic Field

$So, B = {B}_{0}\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}cos\left(\omegat - k\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

The instantaneous force experienced by the particle is:
questions.solution:
Magnetic field vectors associated with this electromagnetic wave are given by
${\overset{\to}{B}}_{1} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c}\overset{^}{k}cos ⁡ \left(kx - \omegat\right)$ & ${\overset{\to}{B}}_{2} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c}\overset{^}{i}cos ⁡ \left(ky - \omegat\right)$
$\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{E} + q\left(\overset{\to}{V} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$

By putting the value of ${\overset{\to}{E}}_{1}, {\overset{\to}{E}}_{2}, {\overset{\to}{B}}_{1} \text{ and } {\overset{\to}{B}}_{2}$
The net Lorentz force on the charged particles is
$\overset{\to}{F} = q{E}_{0}\left[0.8cos ⁡ \left(kx - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{i} + cos\left(ky - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{j} + 0.2cos\left(ky - \omegat\right)\overset{^}{k}\right]$
At $t = 0$ and at $x = y = 0$
$\overset{\to}{F} = q{E}_{0}\left[0.8\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 0.2\overset{^}{k}\right]$

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $25GHz$ is propagating in vacuum along the z-direction. At a particular point in space and time, the magnetic filed is given by $\overset{\to}{B} = 5 \times {10}^{- 8}\overset{^}{j}T .$ The corresponding electric field $\overset{\to}{E}$ is (speed of light $= 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}$ )
questions.solution:
Given, the electromagnetic wave is propagating in $z$ i.e., $+ \overset{^}{k}$ direction.

The relation between the magnitudes of electric field, magnetic field and the speed of light is given by

$\dfrac{\left|E\right|}{\left|B\right|} = C$

$⇒ \left|E\right| = \left|B\right| \times C$
$⇒ \left|E\right| = 5 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 3 \times {10}^{8} = 15V{m}^{- 1}$

We know that the direction of propagation of electromagnetic wave is along $\overset{\to}{E} \times \overset{\to}{B}$.

So, $\overset{\to}{E} = 15\overset{^}{i}V{m}^{- 1}$

similarly
